channel.title: DevPulse · Databases
channel.description: Daily databases stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Postgres 19 slips to November after developers drop up to 10 features
item.description: Postgres 19 is now expected around November 19, with eight to ten significant features deferred after AI review tooling surfaced more bugs than developers could fix. The delay is a useful example of how review capacity and tooling can affect a major database release.

item.title: DuckDB converts JSON text columns into typed columns directly in SQL
item.description: DuckDB can infer and adjust a schema from JSON stored in a VARCHAR column, then produce typed columns without exporting the data to a file. This removes an unnecessary round trip from common analytics and ingestion workflows.

item.title: LLM-assisted review is driving PostgreSQL 19 feature reverts
item.description: PostgreSQL’s beta has seen features reverted over architectural flaws and a long tail of edge-case defects, with LLM-assisted review surfacing issues faster. The resulting workload shows how stronger automated review can raise quality bars while increasing release-management costs.

item.title: Postgres Weekly covers agent-memory results and a queue slowed by savepoints
item.description: The roundup reports that raw conversation retrieval combined with extracted facts beat either alone in a LongMemEval rerun, while per-job savepoints slowed a Postgres queue as workers increased. Both findings offer practical leads for engineers building agent memory or database-backed workloads.

item.title: Iceberg tables are trees of JSON, Avro and Parquet files
item.description: The guide walks through Iceberg metadata, manifest lists, manifests, data files and delete files, showing how DuckDB can inspect each layer with SQL. Understanding that structure helps diagnose slow or incorrect table queries without treating the table as a black box.

item.title: Stripe Data Pipeline adds real-time sync to Postgres
item.description: Stripe Data Pipeline can now keep Postgres databases current with Stripe data, replacing custom sync integrations. The change may simplify the data plumbing behind applications that depend on current payment and account state.

item.title: Pg_vectorsearch adds quantized hierarchical routing for PostgreSQL ANN search
item.description: The alpha PostgreSQL extension combines hierarchical routing, RaBitQ quantization and SIMD distance calculations for approximate nearest-neighbor indexes, with dynamic updates. It could be worth evaluating for vector-search workloads, but the excerpt provides no comparative benchmark results.

item.title: InnoDB row storage favors point reads while indexes add write cost
item.description: The comparison explains that InnoDB stores rows together, making selective reads efficient, while each B-tree index adds work to writes; it also introduces undo logs for concurrent reads and writes. These trade-offs help engineers reason about OLTP and OLAP workload choices.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 beta saw 8–10 significant features reverted
item.description: A PostgreSQL developer reflects on 8–10 significant features reverted after the 19 beta began, including some late in the beta period. The discussion offers lessons for database contributors and teams managing risky releases.

item.title: Postgres TOAST compression can trigger when a value grows by one byte
item.description: The piece shows that a 2,000-byte value remains uncompressed while a 2,001-byte value is compressed to 26 bytes, then explains row-page limits and TOAST behavior. It also covers Postgres 19's shift to LZ4, useful context for storage and compression trade-offs.

item.title: The data cube generalizes SQL aggregation across multiple dimensions
item.description: The paper defines the cube operator as a relational generalization of grouping, cross-tabs, roll-ups, and subtotals, and discusses efficient computation. Its model remains useful context for engineers working on analytical query systems.

item.title: APSW exposes SQLite's full C API to Python
item.description: The wrapper provides SQLite features including virtual tables, VFS, JSON and session support, with synchronous and async usage. It is a useful option when Python applications need more than the standard sqlite3 interface.

item.title: ClickHouse C adds a header-only client for the Native protocol
item.description: The C client decodes ClickHouse Native Format blocks and can read `clickhouse-local` output from a pipe without TCP or compression. Its PostgreSQL-extension-oriented design may interest engineers integrating ClickHouse with other systems.

item.title: JSON tiles accelerate analytics on flexible JSON data
item.description: JSON tiles detect important keys, extract them for relational queries, and collect statistics for the optimizer while supporting changing schemas. The paper reports scan performance similar to columnar storage, a useful approach for semi-structured data systems.

item.title: Project Timestamper cryptographically timestamps Common Crawl’s 339 billion snapshots
item.description: Project Timestamper says it has cryptographically timestamped Common Crawl’s 339 billion web snapshots, spanning 18 years and more than 10 petabytes. Provenance for large web archives matters to engineers working with data at scale.

item.title: DuckLake stores Parquet data with SQL-managed catalog metadata
item.description: The DuckDB extension reads and writes an open lakehouse format that keeps metadata in a catalog database and data in Parquet files. Its SQL-based approach is relevant to engineers evaluating lakehouse storage and query workflows.

item.title: TIN v1.0.6 adds stemming and claims a 2–3× speedup
item.description: The update adds stemming and heap-attribute tiebreakers for top-k ordering; PlanetScale says TIN v1.0.6 is 2–3× faster and has regained the lead in its comparisons. Database engineers evaluating Postgres full-text search can assess the index’s feature and performance claims.

item.title: PostgreSQL separates static query rewrites from data-driven plan optimization
item.description: The piece distinguishes statically knowable rewrites, such as folding `i+0`, from optimization decisions that depend on statistics and data. Understanding that boundary helps engineers reason about query plans and database performance.

item.title: A small DuckDB file can catalog Parquet data without storing it
item.description: DuckDB can hold only view definitions pointing to Parquet files on object storage, creating a shareable catalog that stays a few hundred kilobytes regardless of dataset size. This pattern separates query access from data copies and can simplify sharing data lake datasets.

item.title: Polars 2.0 adds out-of-core support and first-class SQL
item.description: Polars 2.0 adds spill-to-disk support, SQL features, and performance changes; its authors report leading DataFusion and DuckDB on TPC-H and TPC-DS benchmarks. The release is relevant to engineers choosing analytical data engines.

item.title: PlanetScale adds dedicated, configurable read replicas for Postgres
item.description: The replicas asynchronously copy from a primary and can be sized and targeted individually, including in other regions to serve nearby readers. The feature gives engineers another way to distribute read load and reduce latency.

item.title: AlloyDB adds SQL-based fusion for vector and full-text search
item.description: AlloyDB AI combines vector and full-text search results with a SQL function powered by Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and the post also covers the RUM extension for ranking and phrase matching. This can reduce custom fusion and reranking work in RAG systems.

item.title: A Java table function moved analytics data from MongoDB into DuckDB
item.description: After MongoDB-backed analytics and exports slowed, the team moved a year of data into DuckDB and shipped a table function written in Java. The account compares ingestion approaches for engineers weighing analytical workloads alongside operational databases.

item.title: Minigraf combines an embedded graph database with bi-temporal queries
item.description: Minigraf is a single-file graph database with Datalog queries, transaction- and valid-time history, window functions, and native and WASM targets. Its embedded design and temporal graph model may suit agent memory or other applications that need relationship history.

item.title: Doom’s game logic and renderer run in SQL at up to 60 Hz
item.description: The port runs Doom’s game loop at 35 FPS and renders 320×200 frames in SQL, with Python handling input, timing and display; multiplayer works too. It’s an unusual look at pushing a database beyond conventional query workloads.

item.title: Join ordering explores the shape of the query optimizer’s search space
item.description: The piece focuses on join ordering and the dynamic-programming lineage of query optimization, drawing on the author’s study of optimization courses and literature. A stronger mental model of the search space helps engineers reason about query planners and database performance.

item.title: Two stacks support sliding-window aggregation without an inverse
item.description: The piece introduces a two-stack approach for repeated window summaries such as minima, quantiles, and approximate unique counts, where removing an item cannot be handled by an inverse. This is a useful pattern for streaming and telemetry systems.

item.title: Postgres 19 REPACK CONCURRENTLY was fastest in an online rewrite comparison
item.description: A measurement comparing Postgres 19’s REPACK CONCURRENTLY with pg_repack and pg_squeeze found REPACK fastest, while noting trade-offs. The results can inform online table-rewrite choices, though the excerpt does not detail the downsides.
